context.objective: Document how we carry out Manco Treasury & Payment Release, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: Treasury receives the approved payment list. New or changed vendor bank details go through independent callback and sanctions screening first. Only supported, client-approved invoices can enter the payment log. Different authorized users initiate and release the payment in the bank. The exact bank cutoff and individual release limits are not confirmed.
What does Treasury check against the approved payment list and invoices before adding a payment to the log?

For every item we tie vendor, legal entity, amount, currency, payment account and value date or due date back to the approved list and invoice package. We exclude pending queries, duplicates, rejected and unsupported items. Before building the bank instruction we check funding by currency, FX requirements and availability of separate initiator and releaser users. Insufficient funds require an approved funding decision.
When funds are insufficient, what establishes that the funding decision has been approved?

The procedure says to escalate insufficient funds for an approved funding decision. We cannot retry on our own authority. It does not establish the precise authorizer, threshold, form of approval or evidence for a given account. Those are open with Treasury/control and the GPFS owner. The bank releaser separately checks authority in the current access and limit matrix before release.
Who sends Treasury the approved payment list, and what indicates it is ready to process?

The input is MC-01 approved invoices or an approved AP platform list. The AP or payment-run preparer validates it; it is ready only once each invoice has client approval, supporting evidence, and all required details. The document doesn't name one sender for every run. Later the independent releaser checks the bank setup to the invoice and log and records the bank reference, time, initiator, releaser and initial status.
What observable status or event tells Treasury that the payment-release work is complete?

Release alone doesn't close the run. We save bank confirmation with the invoice, update the payment log, monitor exceptions and match the payment log to bank transactions and settled invoices and accounting entries. Released but unsettled, duplicate, returned, missing postings and amount or date differences are investigated. Differences need resolution and reviewer sign-off for each close. The reconciliation schedule, tolerance and exact reviewer remain open.
What can happen to the business or its payees if a payment-release issue is not caught or resolved?

A missed exception can leave a duplicate or returned payment, a vendor unpaid or the ledger inconsistent with bank settlement. We hold the exception open until investigated and reconciled. Insufficient funding is escalated, and retry or recall authority and deadlines remain unconfirmed.
Which role is accountable for the payment run from receipt through reconciliation?
